rows.label: Kingdom of Poland
rows.description: Polish state from the coronation of the first King Bolesław I the Brave in 1025 to the union with Lithuania and the rule of the Jagiellon dynasty in 1385
rows.hook: was ruled by the Piast line and was first crowned under a king nicknamed the Brave

rows.label: Kievan Rus'
rows.description: former federation of East Slavic tribes
rows.hook: was a medieval Slavic realm whose ruler adopted Orthodox Christianity

rows.label: Joseon
rows.description: Korean dynasty / kingdom (1392–1897)
rows.hook: was a long-lived realm that created the native alphabet Hangul

rows.label: Papal States
rows.description: territories mostly in the Appenine Peninsula under the sovereign direct rule of the pope between 756–1870
rows.hook: were lands in the middle of the peninsula ruled directly by the head of the Catholic Church

rows.label: Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt
rows.description: Egyptian state spanning in Hejaz and the Levant (1250–1517)
rows.hook: was ruled by a caste of slave-soldiers who beat back the Mongols at Ain Jalut

rows.label: Kingdom of Bohemia
rows.description: monarchy in Central Europe, predecessor of modern Czech Republic
rows.hook: was a Central European realm within the Holy Roman Empire, ruled for a time by Luxembourg kings

rows.label: Kingdom of Wessex
rows.description: Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the south of Great Britain
rows.hook: was the Anglo-Saxon realm whose king Alfred the Great held off the Vikings

rows.label: Majapahit
rows.description: Empire of Javanese, based in Majakarta (Mojokerto)
rows.hook: was the last great Hindu-Buddhist realm of the Malay Archipelago, remembered for its naval power

rows.label: Benin Empire
rows.description: West African kingdom (1180–1897)
rows.hook: was a West African realm famed for its brass and ivory plaques, many carried off by British troops

rows.label: Khmer Empire
rows.description: 802–1431 empire in Southeast Asia
rows.hook: built the vast temple complex of Angkor Wat

rows.label: Kingdom of Mercia
rows.description: one of the kingdoms of the Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy
rows.hook: was the Anglo-Saxon realm that built Offa's Dyke along its border with Wales

rows.label: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
rows.description: Eastern European monarchical state that existed from 1236 to 1795
rows.hook: grew into one of the largest states in medieval Europe before joining its western neighbour in a commonwealth

rows.label: Kingdom of Navarre
rows.description: Basque medieval kingdom that occupied lands on either side of the western Pyrenees, alongside the Atlantic Ocean (1162–1512)
rows.hook: was a small Basque-led realm in the Pyrenees that straddled the border of France and Spain

rows.label: Duchy of Normandy
rows.description: former European sovereign state, then dukedom of France
rows.hook: was the land granted to Viking chief Rollo, whose descendants later conquered England

rows.label: Ryukyu Kingdom
rows.description: historical kingdom in parts of present-day Japan
rows.hook: was an island realm that grew rich as a trading hub between China and Southeast Asia

rows.label: Srivijaya
rows.description: Empire based on the island of Sumatra from 650 to around 1025
rows.hook: was a Buddhist maritime power that controlled the trade routes through the Strait of Malacca

rows.label: Songhai Empire
rows.description: former state located in western Africa
rows.hook: was the largest West African realm of its time and was centred on the Niger River

rows.label: Grand Principality of Moscow
rows.description: Russian principality (1263–1547)
rows.hook: was the northern state that grew to become the core of the Russian tsars' realm

rows.label: Kingdom of Kongo
rows.description: former African kingdom located in west central Africa
rows.hook: was a Central African realm that traded with Portugal and whose rulers converted to Christianity

rows.label: Latin Empire
rows.description: feudal Crusader state founded by the leaders of the Fourth Crusade on lands captured from the Byzantine Empire
rows.hook: was a Crusader state set up after the Fourth Crusade seized lands from the Byzantines

rows.label: Novgorod Republic
rows.description: Russian city-state (1136–1478)
rows.hook: was a medieval city-state ruled by an assembly called the veche and famed for the hero Alexander Nevsky

rows.label: Empire of Trebizond
rows.description: Byzantine Greek state on Black Sea coast
rows.hook: was a Greek splinter state on the Black Sea that outlived the fall of the Byzantines' capital by decades

rows.label: Emirate of Granada
rows.description: historic Iberian state (1238–1492)
rows.hook: was the last Muslim-ruled realm in Spain, home of the Alhambra palace

rows.label: Republic of Ragusa
rows.description: former maritime republic in southeast Europe (1358–1808)
rows.hook: was a wealthy Adriatic city-state that rivalled Venice in seafaring trade

rows.label: Duchy of Burgundy
rows.description: vassal territory of France, 918–1482
rows.hook: was a rich and powerful realm famed for its wine and its rivalry with the French crown

rows.label: Second Bulgarian Empire
rows.description: Medieval Bulgarian state (1185–1396)
rows.hook: was a medieval Balkan realm that regained independence from the Byzantines before falling to the Ottomans

rows.label: Kingdom of Leon
rows.description: independent medieval kingdom in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula (910–1230), capital León
rows.hook: was a medieval Iberian realm that repeatedly shared its king with its eastern neighbour

rows.label: Tibetan Empire
rows.description: former empire (618–842) centered on the Tibetan Plateau
rows.hook: was a powerful Central Asian realm that spread Buddhism and rivalled Tang China
